title: quick-integrate-stubless-sdk-sprint-notes
body:
Context / problem statement:
- We want a frictionless first-run for internal demos and new customers that doesn’t require a local stub server, docker image, or pre-seeded sandbox. Current starter kits often assume a stub proxy (local/server) which increases cognitive load and failure surface for non-devs.

Goal for this sprint:
- Ship a "stubless" minimal SDK quick-integrate path: single pip/npm install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run a 2-minute sample that streams a chat reply.
- Coverage: JS + Python examples, one small sample app (single-file), basic telemetry enabled (request id, latency, token cost).
- Deliverables: doc + sample code + 3 smoke tests + short runbook for common errors.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Time-to-first-successful-response <= 2 minutes for devs who follow the guide (internal trial with 10 participants).
- First-run failure rate < 15% (errors that prevent a response) during internal dogfood.
- Telemetry shows request_id present and token counts for >= 90% of first-run flows.

Constraints / non-goals:
- Not aiming to replace full sandbox/on-prem flows; this is an onboarding convenience path.
- No production-grade secrets management integration in this sprint (recommend KMS later).

Intended audience:
- Software engineers trying Redwood for the first time, solutions engineers doing quick demos, sales engineers who need a minimal repro. Avoid heavy ops language.

Quickstart (stubless):
1) Install
- Node: npm i -g @redwood/sdk-stubless (placeholder name) or
- Python: pip install redwood-sdk-stubless

2) Set env var (one-liner):
- macOS/Linux: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
- Windows (Powershell): $env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = 'sk_live_xxx'

3) Minimal JS sample (index.js):
- // single-file chat, streams response to STDOUT
- const Redwood = require('@redwood/sdk-stubless')
- const client = new Redwood({mode: 'hosted'})
- async function main(){
-   const res = await client.chat.stream({
-     model: 'rw-v1-small',
-     messages: [{role:'user', content:'Summarize the README in two lines.'}]
-   })
-   for await (const chunk of res) process.stdout.write(chunk)
- }
- main()

4) Minimal Python sample (one file):
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient()
- resp = client.chat.stream(model='rw-v1-small', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Give three onboarding tips.'}])
- for chunk in resp: print(chunk, end='')

5) Run the sample: node index.js OR python quick_chat.py

Developer notes on behavior:
- The stubless SDK will:
  - Default to host=https://api.redwood.ai if REDWOOD_API_URL not set.
  - Implement a small client-side backoff for 429 with jitter (configurable).
  - Stream over SSE/websocket depending on environment; fallback to chunked HTTP.

Telemetry & observability (minimal):
- Include headers and logs we will collect in first-run telemetry:
  - X-Redwood-Request-Id (returned by API)
  - x-client-sdk-version
  - x-local-latency-ms (time from call to first-byte)
- Sample payloads should set metadata: {"run_mode":"quick-integrate","sample_app":"stubless-chat-v1"}
- Emit a short client-side event when first-byte arrives so we can compute cold-start percentiles.

Smoke tests (automated):
- test_smoke_js.sh: installs, env var check mock, run node index.js for 10s, assert output includes expected marker 'SUMMARY:'
- test_smoke_py.sh: same for python sample
- test_telemetry_capture.sh: make a single request and check telemetry endpoint (dev-only) has request_id/token_count present

Common failure modes and runbook (for SEs during demos):
- 401 / invalid api key:
  - symptom: immediate 401, body: "Invalid API key"
  - fix: verify REDWOOD_API_KEY set correctly, ensure no leading/trailing quotes, quick command: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY | wc -c
- Network / TLS errors:
  - symptom: connection refused / CERT_VERIFY_FAILED
  - fix: try curl https://api.redwood.ai/health; if works, inspect corporate TLS interception (common in corp networks).
- Stream stalls / partial output:
  - symptom: some chunks printed but stream ends early
  - fix: increase client timeout to 60s, check proxy buffering (some corp proxies buffer chunked responses).
- 429 / rate limit:
  - symptom: 429 with Retry-After header
  - fix: wait/try again; demo workaround: set model: 'rw-v1-small' to reduce token cost and fallback enabled.

UX copy suggestions for quickstart page:
- Headline: "Two-minute SDK: No local server, no Docker, just your API key."
- Body bullets: "Install. Set your key. Run the sample. Stream a response."
- FAQ snippet: "Why not use the stub?" answer: "Stubs are useful for emulating complex flows; this path optimizes for discovery and speed."

Rollout plan (small, safe):
- Week 0: internal dogfood with SEs and devs (10 people) — collect time-to-first-response and failure reasons.
- Week 1: extend docs with troubleshooting, land PRs, create 3 short screencasts.
- Week 2: enable a lightweight gating flag in Console that exposes a "Try in 1-click" to authenticated SEs (link to demo repo).

Open questions / decisions:
- Rate-limits: do we expose a client-level synthetic backoff policy or keep server-driven only? (Pro: less noisy errors in demos; Con: hides server limits) — decision needed by Nov 20.
- SDK name and package namespace: current working name is '@redwood/sdk-stubless' but branding prefers 'redwood-lite' — need marketing input.
- Telemetry retention for first-run events: default short retention (30d) vs longer (90d) — privacy review required.

Tasks (triageable checklist):
- [ ] Finalize sample code for JS/Python (Marisol)
- [ ] Implement default host fallback and small backoff (Evan)
- [ ] Add telemetry hooks and sample metadata (Lena)
- [ ] Write smoke tests and add to CI dev job (Samir)
- [ ] Draft quickstart doc + screenshots (Marisol)
- [ ] Create 2 short screencasts (SEs) and host on internal drive (Product Ops)

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a tiny client flag --simulate-stub that records request/response pairs locally for later replay (developer convenience) — replay lives outside this sprint.
- For the single-file sample, embed an optional prompt set that demonstrates reranking and then switch to streaming for visual effect.

Appendix: sample troubleshooting commands
- curl health: curl -I https://api.redwood.ai/health
- validate key quickly: node -e "console.log(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY? 'ok':'missing')"
- inspect telemetry: http GET https://telemetry.dev.redwood.ai/q?run_mode=quick-integrate (dev-only)

Last notes:
- Keep language low-friction; assume users are under time pressure (SEs oncalls, lasts-minute demos). Aim for minimal steps and clear fallbacks.
- After dogfood, we will collect verbatim friction points and iterate.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-10 initial outline (Marisol)
- 2024-11-12 added smoke tests and telemetry fields (Evan)
- 2024-11-18 updated runbook and open questions (Marisol)
